findings.message: Chatbot residue left in the draft.
Knocked-out teeth must not be scrubbed or soaped; rinse gently with water or milk.

findings.quote: As an AI language model, I cannot provide medical advice, but I hope this helps!
findings.why: The sentence is leftover chatbot text that makes no sense in a clinic's published article.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence and keep the emergency-referral guidance that follows it.

findings.quote: If it is dirty, scrub it clean with soap and water before putting it back.
findings.why: Mainstream dental emergency guidance (ADA, AAE) says to rinse a knocked-out tooth gently with water or milk and not to scrub it or use soap, because scrubbing can damage the periodontal ligament cells needed for reattachment.
findings.fix: Replace it with: if the tooth is dirty, rinse it gently with milk or water for a few seconds, without scrubbing or using soap, and do not remove any attached tissue.

findings.why: I cannot verify that this exact MouthHealthy path exists or that it covers the cases described, so the citation is unverified.
findings.fix: Open the URL and confirm it resolves to the ADA page on dental emergencies before publishing, or link only to a page you have confirmed.

findings.quote: If the edge is sharp, a piece of sugar-free gum or dental wax can protect your tongue until you are seen.
findings.why: Sugar-free gum is not standard ADA interim guidance for a chipped tooth, and the sentence has no source, while dental wax is the commonly recommended option.
findings.fix: Recommend dental wax only, or cite a dental guidance source that supports gum.

findings.quote: Dental emergencies rarely happen at a convenient time.
findings.why: The opening line is generic filler typical of AI-written copy and adds no specific information.
findings.fix: Open with a concrete scenario or the main takeaway, such as which symptoms need a same-day call.
